Is the muxed counter latched into MUX_COUNT? (Scenario: The host writes to SNAPSHOT at address 0x03C (not exactly 0x038, but within the register region, data 0) .) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: No. 0x03C is not a mapped register (the last mapped address is 0x038), so the write is ignored and MUX_COUNT is not latched. Only a write to 0x038 triggers SNAPSHOT.
questions.evidence: Unmapped addresses read 0 and ignore writes.

questions.text: After reset release, what are BUSY and DONE: both 0, BUSY 0 with DONE 1, or measurement continues? (Scenario: A frequency measurement with GATE_LEN 25,000,000 is running (BUSY=1) when the internal power-on reset is asserted again, 10,000,000 clk_c3 cycles after START.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Both BUSY and DONE are 0 after reset release. The reset values list FREQ_STATUS as 0, which clears BUSY (bit 0) and DONE (bit 1), so the measurement does not continue.
questions.evidence: - Reset: SEL 0 (clock A), GATE_LEN 25,000,000, SWITCH_COUNT 0, MUX_ERRS 0, STATUS 0, FREQ_STATUS 0, FREQ_COUNT 0.

questions.text: How many clk_c3 cycles after the START write does BUSY first read 1, and does DONE become 1 at gate end (answer the number of clk_c3 cycles BUSY stays 1)? (Scenario: GATE_LEN is set to 1 and START is written once.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?

By how much does SWITCH_COUNT increase in total, and is that determined by the requirements (answer the increase as a number)? (Scenario: While SEL=0 and ACTIVE_SEL=0, the host writes SEL=1, and 3 clk_c3 clocks later (switch still in progress, ACTIVE_SEL still 0) writes SEL=0.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: SWITCH_COUNT increases by 2. The first write (SEL=1) starts a switch to B, and it is never aborted, so it completes and counts once. The second write (SEL=0) arrives while SWITCHING is 1, so it is queued. When the first switch ends, the queued value 0 differs from the current selection (B), so it is acted on as a real switch back to A, which completes and counts once more. The requirements settle this.
questions.evidence: A write to SEL while SWITCHING is 1 is queued: the last value written wins and is acted on when the current switch ends (a switch is never aborted).

questions.text: Does h_rdata show 0xAAAA5555 for that read? (Scenario: The host pulses h_we writing 0xAAAA5555 to SCRATCH at clk_c3 cycle N, then pulses h_re for SCRATCH at cycle N+1.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: Yes. SCRATCH reads back what was written, and the write takes effect the clock after h_we. That is the same clock as the h_re pulse at N+1, and h_rdata only has to show the register within 2 clocks of h_re. So h_rdata must show 0xAAAA5555 for that read and hold it.
questions.evidence: | 0x008 | SCRATCH | RW | 32 bits, reads back what was written, resets to 0 |

questions.text: Does the running gate restart (gate end moves later)? (Scenario: The host writes FREQ_CTRL.START=1 while a measurement is already BUSY=1, 5,000,000 cycles into a default gate.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: No. FREQ_CTRL.START is ignored while BUSY, so the running gate does not restart and its end does not move later.

questions.text: What is SWITCH_COUNT after the switch completes and settles? (Scenario: SEL=0 active. SEL is written 1 (switch starts). While SWITCHING is 1, SEL is written 1 again, then the switch completes. SWITCH_COUNT was 0 before.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: SWITCH_COUNT is 1. The first write to SEL starts one switch, which increments SWITCH_COUNT on completion. The second write of 1 is queued, and the last value written wins. When the switch ends, ACTIVE_SEL already equals 1, so the queued value is the same as the current selection. A same-value write is not a switch, so no second switch occurs.
questions.evidence: A write to SEL while SWITCHING is 1 is queued: the last value written wins and is acted on when the current switch ends (a switch is never aborted).
